mcqs.explanation:
Independent (Subordinate Clause) - Subordinate Clause: Does not express a complete thought and depends on the independent clause for its meaning. Subordinate Clause, such a clause becomes which does not express a complete thought and depends on the independent clause for its meaning. Example 1. When the manager arrived we started the meeting. (Dependent Clause Independent Clause) 2. I continued working although I was tired. (Independent Clause Dependent Clause)

Kinds of Subordinate Clauses:
1. Noun Clause – Functions as a Noun (Subject/Object/Complement)
Ex.1. What they say is true. (Noun Clause used as Subject)
2. I know that she is honest. (Noun Clause used as Object)
3. Her belief is that she will win. (Noun Clause as Complement)

2. Adjective Clause (Relative Clause) – Modifies a Noun or pronoun.
Ex. 1. The building that was constructed last year has collapsed. (Adjective Clause qualifying building)
2. The girl who won the prize is very intelligent. (Adjective Clause qualifying girl)

3. Adverb Clause – Modifies a Verb, adjective, or another Adverb.
Ex. 1. I will come when you call me. (Adverb Clause qualifying come)
2. Lucy succeeded because she worked hard. (Adverb Clause qualifying succeeded)

4. Infinitive Clause – A clause that begins with (to + V1) used as a Subject, object, or to show purpose, after wh- words, after adjectives in goal.
Ex. 1. To win the match was their main goal. (Infinitive Clause as a subject)
2. He works hard to earn money. (Infinitive Clause to show purpose)

Practice Questions
1. What he said was completely true and based on logical reasoning during the discussion session.
(a) Adjective Clause (b) Adverb Clause (c) Noun Clause (d) Infinitive Clause

2. She did not understand why he left the meeting abruptly without informing anyone.
(a) Adjective Clause (b) Adverb Clause (c) Noun Clause (d) Infinitive Clause

3. The student who secured the highest marks in the examination was awarded a scholarship.
(a) Noun Clause (b) Adjective Clause (c) Adverb Clause (d) Infinitive Clause

4. The match was postponed because it was raining heavily throughout the evening in the entire day.
(a) Noun Clause (b) Adjective Clause (c) Adverb Clause (d) None

5. If the authorities had taken appropriate measures at the right time, the situation would not have become so critical in the affected areas.
(a) Noun Clause (b) Adjective Clause (c) Adverb Clause (d) None

6. He will come when you call him.
(a) Noun Clause (b) Adjective Clause (c) Adverb Clause (d) Infinitive Clause

7. Although he was tired, he continued working.
(a) Noun Clause (b) Adjective Clause (c) Adverb Clause (d) Infinitive Clause

8. The committee could not decide whether the proposal should be approved immediately or reviewed again later.
(a) Noun Clause (b) Adjective Clause (c) Adverb Clause (d) Main Clause

9. Karan remained uncertain about whether the information provided to him was accurate.
(a) Noun Clause (b) Adjective Clause (c) Adverb Clause (d) Prepositional

10. Once dense forests, which acted as vital carbon sinks and habitats for myriad species, are now alarmingly fragmented.
(SSC CHSL, 2025)
(a) Adjective clause (b) Adverb clause (c) Noun clause (d) Prepositional clause

11. The government's decision, which was strongly criticized by several economists, created uncertainty in the financial market.
(a) Noun Clause (b) Adjective Clause (c) Adverb Clause (d) Coordinate Clause

12. "Digital platforms, when judiciously curated, can also serve as catalysts for mental growth" the phrase "when judiciously curated" functions as:
(SSC CHSL, 2025)
(a) Noun clause (b) Adverbial clause of time (c) Adjective clause (d) Absolute phrase

13. "The mechanical extraction of minerals may cause irreversible damage to species uniquely adapted to these high-pressure, low-light environments many of which remain undiscovered," the clause "many of which remain undiscovered" is an example of which type of clause?
(SSC CGL, 2025)
(a) Adverbial clause (b) Noun clause (c) Relative clause (d) Conditional clause

14. Yet, over time, anomalies that cannot be explained within the current paradigm accumulate.
(SSC Phase XIII, 2025)
(a) Noun clause (b) Adverbial clause (c) Relative clause (d) Independent clause
